sanskrit: rāmasya tu vacaḥ śrutvā muniveṣadharaṃ ca tam samīkṣya saha bhāryābhī rājā vigatacetanaḥ
english: Having heard Rāma's words and having seen him clad in the garb of an ascetic, the king, together with his wives, lost all consciousness.

sanskrit: nainaṃ duḥkhena saṃtaptaḥ pratyavaikṣata rāghavam na cainam abhisaṃprekṣya pratyabhāṣata durmanāḥ
english: Tormented by grief, he could not look upon that Rāghava, nor, gazing at him, could he bring himself to speak — so wretched was he in his mind.

sanskrit: sa muhūrtam ivāsaṃjño duḥkhitaś ca mahīpatiḥ vilalāpa mahābāhū rāmam evānucintayan
english: For a moment that lord of the earth, afflicted and senseless, lamented, his great arms hanging limp, his thoughts fixed on Rāma alone.

sanskrit: manye khalu mayā pūrvaṃ vivatsā bahavaḥ kṛtāḥ prāṇino hiṃsitā vāpi tasmād idam upasthitam
english: "Surely in a former life I must have separated many creatures from their young, or else slain living beings — and therefore this calamity has come upon me."

sanskrit: na tv evānāgate kāle dehāc cyavati jīvitam kaikeyyā kliśyamānasya mṛtyur mama na vidyate
english: "Yet the life-breath does not depart the body before its appointed hour; even as I am tormented by Kaikeyī, death does not find me."

sanskrit: yo 'haṃ pāvakasaṃkāśaṃ paśyāmi purataḥ sthitam vihāya vasane sūkṣme tāpasācchādam ātmajam
english: "I who look upon my own son standing before me, radiant as fire, having set aside his fine garments for the dress of an ascetic —"

sanskrit: ekasyāḥ khalu kaikeyyāḥ kṛte 'yaṃ kliśyate janaḥ svārthe prayatamānāyāḥ saṃśritya nikṛtiṃ tv imām
english: "For the sake of one woman alone — Kaikeyī — who strives for her own ends and has resorted to this base deception, all this people suffers."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu vacanaṃ bāṣpeṇa pihitekṣṇaha rāmeti sakṛd evoktvā vyāhartuṃ na śaśāka ha
english: Having spoken these words, his eyes sealed shut with tears, he uttered once only the name "Rāma" and could speak no more.

sanskrit: saṃjñāṃ tu pratilabhyaiva muhūrtāt sa mahīpatiḥ netrābhyām aśrupūrṇābhyāṃ sumantram idam abravīt
english: After a moment that king of the earth recovered his senses and, with eyes brimming with tears, spoke these words to Sumantra:

sanskrit: aupavāhyaṃ rathaṃ yuktvā tvam āyāhi hayottamaiḥ prāpayainaṃ mahābhāgam ito janapadāt param
english: "Harness the royal chariot with the finest horses and come; convey this most fortunate one beyond the boundaries of this kingdom."

sanskrit: evaṃ manye guṇavatāṃ guṇānāṃ phalam ucyate pitrā mātrā ca yat sādhur vīro nirvāsyate vanam
english: "Such, I believe, is said to be the fruit of virtue for the virtuous — that a righteous hero is banished to the forest by both his father and his mother."

sanskrit: rājño vacanam ājñāya sumantraḥ śīghravikramaḥ yojayitvāyayau tatra ratham aśvair alaṃkṛtam
english: Understanding the king's command, Sumantra, swift of movement, harnessed the chariot adorned with horses and drove it there.

sanskrit: taṃ rathaṃ rājaputrāya sūtaḥ kanakabhūṣitam ācacakṣe 'ñjaliṃ kṛtvā yuktaṃ paramavājibhiḥ
english: The charioteer, joining his palms together, announced to the prince that chariot adorned with gold and yoked with the finest steeds.

sanskrit: rājā satvaram āhūya vyāpṛtaṃ vittasaṃcaye uvāca deśakālajño niścitaṃ sarvataḥ śuci
english: The king, knowing time and place, quickly summoned the treasurer who was engaged in the management of the treasury and spoke to him clearly, with full resolution.

sanskrit: vāsāṃsi ca mahārhāṇi bhūṣaṇāni varāṇi ca varṣāṇy etāni saṃkhyāya vaidehyāḥ kṣipram ānaya
english: "Count out the years of her exile and bring quickly the most precious garments and the finest ornaments befitting Vaidehī."

sanskrit: narendreṇaivam uktas tu gatvā kośagṛhaṃ tataḥ prāyacchat sarvam āhṛtya sītāyai kṣipram eva tat
english: Thus addressed by the king, the treasurer went to the treasury and, having brought everything, gave it all immediately to Sītā.

sanskrit: sā sujātā sujātāni vaidehī prasthitā vanam bhūṣayām āsa gātrāṇi tair vicitrais vibhūṣaṇaiḥ
english: She who was born of noble lineage, Vaidehī, setting forth for the forest, adorned her graceful limbs with those many-coloured ornaments.

sanskrit: vyarājayata vaidehī veśma tat suvibhūṣitā udyato 'ṃśumataḥ kāle khaṃ prabheva vivasvataḥ
english: Vaidehī, thus richly adorned, illumined that palace as the radiance of the rising sun illumines the sky at the hour of dawn.

sanskrit: tāṃ bhujābhyāṃ pariṣvajya śvaśrūr vacanam abravīt anācarantīṃ kṛpaṇaṃ mūdhny upāghrāya maithilīm
english: Her mother-in-law embraced her in both arms, kissed her on the crown of the head, and spoke, even as Maithilī showed no sign of despair:

sanskrit: asatyaḥ sarvaloke 'smin satataṃ satkṛtāḥ priyaiḥ bhartāraṃ nānumanyante vinipātagataṃ striyaḥ
english: "In this entire world, women who are constantly honoured and pampered by their dear ones do not follow their husbands when they fall upon misfortune — such women are false."

sanskrit: sa tvayā nāvamantavyaḥ putraḥ pravrājito mama tava daivatam astv eṣa nirdhanaḥ sadhano 'pi vā
english: "My son who has been sent into exile must not be slighted by you; whether he be penniless or wealthy, let him be your deity."

sanskrit: vijñāya vacanaṃ sītā tasyā dharmārthasaṃhitam kṛtāñjalir uvācedaṃ śvaśrūm abhimukhe sthitā
english: Understanding her mother-in-law's words, which were rooted in righteousness and truth, Sītā stood before her, folded her palms, and replied:

sanskrit: kariṣye sarvam evāham āryā yad anuśāsti mām abhijñāsmi yathā bhartur vartitavyaṃ śrutaṃ ca me
english: "I shall do all that the noble lady instructs me. I know well how one ought to conduct oneself toward one's husband — this I have heard and learnt."

sanskrit: na mām asajjanenāryā samānayitum arhati dharmād vicalituṃ nāham alaṃ candrād iva prabhā
english: "The noble lady need not count me among ignoble women. I am no more capable of straying from dharma than moonlight is of straying from the moon."

sanskrit: nātantrī vādyate vīṇā nācakro vartate rathaḥ nāpatiḥ sukham edhate yā syād api śatātmajā
english: "A vīṇā without its strings does not sound; a chariot without its wheel does not move; a wife does not flourish in happiness without her husband, even if she has a hundred sons."

sanskrit: mitaṃ dadāti hi pitā mitaṃ mātā mitaṃ sutaḥ amitasya hi dātāraṃ bhartāraṃ kā na pūjayet
english: "A father gives in measure; a mother gives in measure; a son gives in measure — but a husband gives without measure. What woman would not revere such a giver?"

sanskrit: sāham evaṃgatā śreṣṭhā śrutadharmaparāvarā ārye kim avamanyeyaṃ strīṇāṃ bhartā hi daivatam
english: "Being thus, I am the best, well-versed in the highest and lowest teachings of dharma. Noble lady, why should I dishonour my husband? For a husband is indeed the deity of women."

sanskrit: sītāyā vacanaṃ śrutvā kausalyā hṛdayaṃgamam śuddhasattvā mumocāśru sahasā duḥkhaharṣajam
english: Having heard Sītā's words, which touched the heart, Kausalyā — pure of nature — suddenly shed tears born at once of sorrow and of joy.

sanskrit: tāṃ prāñjalir abhikramya mātṛmadhye 'tisatkṛtām rāmaḥ paramadharmajño mātaraṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Then Rāma, supremely versed in dharma, drew near with joined palms to his mother who was honoured above all among the mothers, and addressed her:

sanskrit: amba mā duḥkhitā bhūs tvaṃ paśya tvaṃ pitaraṃ mama kṣayo hi vanavāsasya kṣipram eva bhaviṣyati
english: "Mother, do not grieve. Attend to my father. The period of forest exile will come to an end swiftly."

sanskrit: suptāyās te gamiṣyanti navavarṣāṇi pañca ca sā samagram iha prāptaṃ māṃ drakṣyasi suhṛdvṛtam
english: "The fourteen years will pass for you as if in sleep, and you shall see me returned here, complete, surrounded by friends."

sanskrit: etāvad abhinītārtham uktvā sa jananīṃ vacaḥ trayaḥ śataśatārdhā hi dadarśāvekṣya mātaraḥ
english: Having spoken these words of well-measured meaning to his mother, he looked and beheld the three hundred and fifty mothers gathered there.

sanskrit: tāś cāpi sa tathaivārtā mātṝr daśarathātmajaḥ dharmayuktam idaṃ vākyaṃ nijagāda kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: To those mothers, equally distressed, the son of Daśaratha spoke this righteous word with palms joined together:

sanskrit: saṃvāsāt paruṣaṃ kiṃ cid ajñānād vāpi yat kṛtam tan me samanujānīta sarvāś cāmantrayāmi vaḥ
english: "Whatever harsh thing has been done by me from living together in close quarters, or from ignorance, please forgive me all of it — and I take leave of you all."

sanskrit: jajñe 'tha tāsāṃ saṃnādaḥ krauñcīnām iva niḥsvanaḥ mānavendrasya bhāryāṇām evaṃ vadati rāghave
english: Then, as Rāghava spoke thus, a wail arose from those wives of the lord of men — like the cry of krauñca cranes.

sanskrit: murajapaṇavameghaghoṣavad daśarathaveśma babhūva yat purā vilapita paridevanākulaṃ vyasanagataṃ tad abhūt suduḥkhitam
english: The mansion of Daśaratha, which had once resounded like the rumble of murajas and paṇavas and thunder-clouds, now became utterly wretched, filled with lament and wailing, plunged into calamity.

sanskrit: atha rāmaś ca sītā ca lakṣmaṇaś ca kṛtāñjaliḥ upasaṃgṛhya rājānaṃ cakrur dīnāḥ pradakṣiṇam
english: Then Rāma, Sītā, and Lakṣmaṇa, with joined palms, embraced the king and, pitifully, performed the rite of circumambulation around him.

sanskrit: taṃ cāpi samanujñāpya dharmajñaḥ sītayā saha rāghavaḥ śokasaṃmūḍho jananīm abhyavādayat
english: Having obtained the king's leave, Rāghava, the knower of dharma, dazed with grief, then paid obeisance to his mother together with Sītā.

sanskrit: anvakṣaṃ lakṣmaṇo bhrātuḥ kausalyām abhyavādayat atha mātuḥ sumitrāyā jagrāha caraṇau punaḥ
english: After his brother, Lakṣmaṇa paid obeisance to Kausalyā, and then in turn clasped the feet of his own mother Sumitrā.

sanskrit: taṃ vandamānaṃ rudatī mātā saumitrim abravīt hitakāmā mahābāhuṃ mūrdhny upāghrāya lakṣmaṇam
english: His mother, weeping, wishing his good, kissed Lakṣmaṇa of the mighty arms on the crown of the head as he bowed, and spoke to the son of Sumitrā:

sanskrit: sṛṣṭas tvaṃ vanavāsāya svanuraktaḥ suhṛjjane rāme pramādaṃ mā kārṣīḥ putra bhrātari gacchati
english: "You were born for this forest sojourn, deeply devoted to those dear to you. Son, be not heedless toward Rāma as your elder brother proceeds on his way."

sanskrit: vyasanī vā samṛddho vā gatir eṣa tavānagha eṣa loke satāṃ dharmo yaj jyeṣṭhavaśago bhavet
english: "Whether he be in adversity or in prosperity, he is your refuge, O sinless one. This is the dharma of the good in this world — to be obedient to one's elder brother."

sanskrit: idaṃ hi vṛttam ucitaṃ kulasyāsya sanātanam dānaṃ dīkṣā ca yajñeṣu tanutyāgo mṛdheṣu ca
english: "This is the eternal, fitting conduct of this lineage: giving, consecration in sacrifices, and the offering of one's body in battle."

sanskrit: rāmaṃ daśarathaṃ viddhi māṃ viddhi janakātmajām ayodhyām aṭavīṃ viddhi gaccha tāta yathāsukham
english: "Know Rāma as Daśaratha, know me as Janaka's daughter, know the forest as Ayodhyā — go, dear child, at your ease."

sanskrit: tataḥ sumantraḥ kākutsthaṃ prāñjalir vākyam abravīt vinīto vinayajñaś ca mātalir vāsavaṃ yathā
english: Then Sumantra, humble and well-versed in courtesy — as Mātali addresses Vāsava — spoke to that scion of the Kākutstha line with joined palms:

sanskrit: ratham āroha bhadraṃ te rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ kṣipraṃ tvāṃ prāpayiṣyāmi yatra māṃ rāma vakṣyasi
english: "Mount the chariot — good fortune to you, O prince of great renown. I shall swiftly convey you, Rāma, wherever you direct me."

sanskrit: caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi vastavyāni vane tvayā tāny upakramitavyāni yāni devyāsi coditaḥ
english: "For fourteen years are to be spent by you in the forest; those years must now be entered upon, as the queen has urged upon you."

sanskrit: taṃ rathaṃ sūryasaṃkāśaṃ sītā hṛṣṭena cetasā āruroha varārohā kṛtvālaṃkāram ātmanaḥ
english: Sītā, that noble lady, adorned herself and then, with a joyful heart, mounted that chariot resplendent as the sun.

sanskrit: tathaivāyudhajātāni bhrātṛbhyāṃ kavacāni ca rathopasthe pratinyasya sacarmakaṭhinaṃ ca tat
english: Likewise the two brothers placed in the body of the chariot all manner of weapons, their armour, and the leather quivers with their hard casings.

sanskrit: sītātṛtīyān ārūḍhān dṛṣṭvā dhṛṣṭam acodayat sumantraḥ saṃmatān aśvān vāyuvegasamāñ jave
english: Having seen the three — Rāma, Sītā, and Lakṣmaṇa — mounted, Sumantra boldly urged on the chosen horses, swift as the wind in their speed.

sanskrit: prayāte tu mahāraṇyaṃ cirarātrāya rāghave babhūva nagare mūrcchā balamūrcchā janasya ca
english: But as Rāghava set out for the great forest for so many long nights, a swoon fell over the city, a swoon fell over the army and the people alike.

sanskrit: tat samākulasaṃbhrāntaṃ mattasaṃkupita dvipam hayaśiñjitanirghoṣaṃ puram āsīn mahāsvanam
english: That city, thrown into confusion and agitation, resounded with great noise — the trumpeting of frenzied elephants and the jingling of horses.

sanskrit: tataḥ sabālavṛddhā sā purī paramapīḍitā rāmam evābhidudrāva gharmārtaḥ salilaṃ yathā
english: Then that city — young and old together — stricken with extreme anguish, rushed after Rāma alone, as the heat-parched earth rushes toward water.

sanskrit: pārśvataḥ pṛṣṭhataś cāpi lambamānās tadunmukhāḥ bāṣpapūrṇamukhāḥ sarve tam ūcur bhṛśaduḥkhitāḥ
english: Clinging to the sides and the rear of the chariot, all faces turned toward him, their faces filled with tears, all spoke to him in deep distress:

sanskrit: saṃyaccha vājināṃ raśmīn sūta yāhi śanaiḥ śanaiḥ mukhaṃ drakṣyāmi rāmasya durdarśaṃ no bhaviṣyati
english: "Hold back the reins of the horses, charioteer — drive slowly, slowly! I would behold Rāma's face, which shall be hard for us to see again."

sanskrit: āyasaṃ hṛdayaṃ nūnaṃ rāmamātur asaṃśayam yad devagarbhapratime vanaṃ yāti na bhidyate
english: "Surely the heart of Rāma's mother must be made of iron, since it does not break even as one who is like the offspring of a god goes to the forest."

sanskrit: kṛtakṛtyā hi vaidehī chāyevānugatā patim na jahāti ratā dharme merum arkaprabhā yathā
english: "Vaidehī has truly accomplished her life's purpose — like a shadow she follows her husband, she who is devoted to dharma forsakes him not, as the sun's radiance does not forsake Mount Meru."

sanskrit: aho lakṣmaṇa siddhārthaḥ satatāṃ priyavādinam bhrātaraṃ devasaṃkāśaṃ yas tvaṃ paricariṣyasi
english: "O Lakṣmaṇa, you have achieved your purpose, you who shall attend upon your brother who is ever kind in speech and radiant as a god."

sanskrit: mahaty eṣā hi te siddhir eṣa cābhyudayo mahān eṣa svargasya mārgaś ca yad enam anugacchasi evaṃ vadantas te soḍhuṃ na śekur bāṣpam āgatam
english: "This indeed is a great achievement for you; this is a great rise of fortune; this is the very path to heaven — that you follow him." So saying, those people could not hold back the tears that had come upon them.

sanskrit: atha rājā vṛtaḥ strībhir dīnābhir dīnacetanaḥ nirjagāma priyaṃ putraṃ drakṣyāmīti bruvan gṛhāt
english: Then the king, his spirit utterly desolate, surrounded by wretched women, came forth from the palace, saying "I will see my dear son."

sanskrit: śuśruve cāgrataḥ strīṇāṃ rudantīnāṃ mahāsvanaḥ yathā nādaḥ kareṇūnāṃ baddhe mahati kuñjare
english: And ahead of him was heard the great wailing of the women weeping — like the cry of she-elephants when a great bull elephant is bound in chains.

sanskrit: pitā ca rājā kākutsthaḥ śrīmān sannas tadā babhau paripūrṇaḥ śaśī kāle graheṇopapluto yathā
english: And the father, that glorious king of the Kākutstha line, appeared at that moment stricken and diminished — like the full moon at the appointed time swallowed by a eclipse.

sanskrit: tato halahalāśabdo jajñe rāmasya pṛṣṭhataḥ narāṇāṃ prekṣya rājānaṃ sīdantaṃ bhṛśaduḥkhitam
english: Then a great tumult of wailing arose behind Rāma as the people looked upon the king sinking under his terrible grief.

sanskrit: hā rāmeti janāḥ ke cid rāmamāteti cāpare antaḥpuraṃ samṛddhaṃ ca krośantaṃ paryadevayan
english: Some among the people cried "Ah, Rāma!" and others cried "Ah, Rāma's mother!" — and the prosperous inner palace lamented and wept all around.

sanskrit: anvīkṣamāṇo rāmas tu viṣaṇṇaṃ bhrāntacetasaṃ rājānaṃ mātaraṃ caiva dadarśānugatau pathi dharmapāśena saṃkṣiptaḥ prakāśaṃ nābhyudaikṣata
english: As Rāma looked back he saw the king — dejected, his mind reeling — and his mother both following along the road; bound by the bonds of dharma, he could not openly look upon them.

sanskrit: padātinau ca yānārhāv aduḥkhārhau sukhocitau dṛṣṭvā saṃcodayām āsa śīghraṃ yāhīti sārathim
english: Seeing those two who deserved to ride in a vehicle, who deserved no sorrow and were accustomed to happiness, now proceeding on foot, he urged the charioteer: "Drive swiftly!"

sanskrit: na hi tat puruṣavyāghro duḥkhadaṃ darśanaṃ pituḥ mātuś ca sahituṃ śaktas totrārdita iva dvipaḥ
english: For that tiger among men could not endure that painful sight of his father and mother — as an elephant cannot endure the goad.

sanskrit: tathā rudantīṃ kausalyāṃ rathaṃ tam anudhāvatīm krośantīṃ rāma rāmeti hā sīte lakṣmaṇeti ca asakṛt praikṣata tadā nṛtyantīm iva mātaram
english: Again and again he looked back at Kausalyā weeping and running after that chariot, crying "Rāma! Rāma!" and "Ah, Sītā! Lakṣmaṇa!" — his mother then appeared to him as though she were dancing.

sanskrit: tiṣṭheti rājā cukroṣa yāhi yāhīti rāghavaḥ sumantrasya babhūvātmā cakrayor iva cāntarā
english: The king cried out "Stop!" while Rāghava called out "Drive on! Drive on!" — and Sumantra's spirit was caught between the two, as between the two wheels of a chariot.

sanskrit: nāśrauṣam iti rājānam upālabdho 'pi vakṣyasi ciraṃ duḥkhasya pāpiṣṭham iti rāmas tam abravīt
english: "Even if you are reproached, you can say to the king: 'I did not hear' — for this deception, long the cause of suffering, is the least sinful course," so Rāma spoke to him.

sanskrit: rāmasya sa vacaḥ kurvann anujñāpya ca taṃ janam vrajato 'pi hayāñ śīghraṃ codayām āsa sārathiḥ
english: Acting on Rāma's word and taking leave of those people, the charioteer urged on the horses to speed, even as they were already in motion.

sanskrit: nyavartata jano rājño rāmaṃ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇam manasāpy aśruvegaiś ca na nyavartata mānuṣam
english: The people of the king turned back after circumambulating Rāma — yet in their hearts, and in the rush of their tears, no human being turned back.

sanskrit: yam icchet punar āyāntaṃ nainaṃ dūram anuvrajet ity amātyā mahārājam ūcur daśarathaṃ vacaḥ
english: "One who wishes him to return should not follow him far" — thus the ministers spoke their word to the great king Daśaratha.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ vacaḥ sarvaguṇopapannaṃ prasvinnagātraḥ praviṣaṇṇarūpaḥ niśamya rājā kṛpaṇaḥ sabhāryo vyavasthitas taṃ sutam īkṣamāṇaḥ
english: Hearing their words, endowed with every quality, the wretched king — his body bathed in sweat, his appearance sunken — stood still together with his wife, his eyes fixed upon his son.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu puruṣavyāghre niṣkrāmati kṛtāñjalau ārtaśabdo hi saṃjajñe strīṇām antaḥpure mahān
english: When that tiger among men departed with his palms joined, a great cry of anguish arose from the women in the inner apartments.

sanskrit: anāthasya janasyāsya durbalasya tapasvinaḥ yo gatiṃ śaraṇaṃ cāsīt sa nāthaḥ kva nu gacchati
english: "He who was the resort and refuge of this helpless, weak, and afflicted people — where now does that protector go?"

sanskrit: na krudhyaty abhiśasto 'pi krodhanīyāni varjayan kruddhān prasādayan sarvān samaduḥkhaḥ kva gacchati
english: "He who does not grow angry even when falsely accused, who avoids all occasions of wrath, who appeases those who are wrathful, who regards the suffering of others as his own — where does he go?"

sanskrit: kausalyāyāṃ mahātejā yathā mātari vartate tathā yo vartate 'smāsu mahātmā kva nu gacchati
english: "He of great splendour, that great-souled one, who conducts himself toward us exactly as he conducts himself toward his mother Kausalyā — where does he now go?"

sanskrit: kaikeyyā kliśyamānena rājñā saṃcodito vanam paritrātā janasyāsya jagataḥ kva nu gacchati
english: "Urged to the forest by a king tormented by Kaikeyī — he who was the protector of these people and of the world — where does he now go?"

sanskrit: aho niścetano rājā jīvalokasya saṃpriyam dharmyaṃ satyavrataṃ rāmaṃ vanavāso pravatsyati
english: "Alas, the king is without wisdom — Rāma, beloved of all the living world, devoted to dharma and to the vow of truth, will now dwell in forest exile!"

sanskrit: iti sarvā mahiṣyas tā vivatsā iva dhenavaḥ ruruduś caiva duḥkhārtāḥ sasvaraṃ ca vicukruśuḥ
english: Thus all those great queens, afflicted with sorrow, wept and wailed aloud, like cows that have lost their calves.

sanskrit: sa tam antaḥpure ghoram ārtaśabdaṃ mahīpatiḥ putraśokābhisaṃtaptaḥ śrutvā cāsīt suduḥkhitaḥ
english: The lord of the earth, already scorched by grief for his son, heard that terrible cry of anguish from the inner apartments and was plunged into yet deeper sorrow.

sanskrit: nāgnihotrāṇy ahūyanta sūryaś cāntaradhīyata vyasṛjan kavalān nāgā gāvo vatsān na pāyayan
english: The sacred agnihotra fires were not kindled; the sun seemed to disappear; elephants dropped their mouthfuls of food; cows did not suckle their calves.

sanskrit: triśaṅkur lohitāṅgaś ca bṛhaspatibudhāv api dāruṇāḥ somam abhyetya grahāḥ sarve vyavasthitāḥ
english: Triśaṅku, the red-limbed one (Mars), Bṛhaspati, and Budha too — all the planets, malefic, drew close to the Moon and stood there in dreadful conjunction.

sanskrit: nakṣatrāṇi gatārcīṃṣi grahāś ca gatatejasaḥ viśākhāś ca sadhūmāś ca nabhasi pracakāśire
english: The nakṣatras lost their radiance and the planets lost their lustre; Viśākhā herself appeared in the sky shrouded in smoke.

sanskrit: akasmān nāgaraḥ sarvo jano dainyam upāgamat āhāre vā vihāre vā na kaś cid akaron manaḥ
english: Suddenly all the townspeople fell into a state of dejection; no one applied his mind either to eating or to recreation.

sanskrit: bāṣpaparyākulamukho rājamārgagato janaḥ na hṛṣṭo lakṣyate kaś cit sarvaḥ śokaparāyaṇaḥ
english: The people moving along the royal road had faces clouded with tears; not one person was to be seen with joy — all were given over entirely to grief.

sanskrit: na vāti pavanaḥ śīto na śaśī saumyadarśanaḥ na sūryas tapate lokaṃ sarvaṃ paryākulaṃ jagat
english: The cool wind did not blow; the moon did not show its gentle face; the sun gave no warmth to the world — the entire universe was thrown into confusion.

sanskrit: anarthinaḥ sutāḥ strīṇāṃ bhartāro bhrātaras tathā sarve sarvaṃ parityajya rāmam evānvacintayan
english: Sons indifferent to their mothers, husbands indifferent to their wives, brothers indifferent to their brothers — all, abandoning everything, thought only of Rāma.

sanskrit: ye tu rāmasya suhṛdaḥ sarve te mūḍhacetasaḥ śokabhāreṇa cākrāntāḥ śayanaṃ na juhus tadā
english: Those who were friends of Rāma had all become bewildered in mind; overwhelmed by the weight of grief, they did not then resort to their beds.

sanskrit: tatas tv ayodhyā rahitā mahātmanā puraṃdareṇeva mahī saparvatā cacāla ghoraṃ bhayabhārapīḍitā sanāgayodhāśvagaṇā nanāda ca
english: Then Ayodhyā, bereft of that great-souled one — as the earth bereft of Indra — shook terribly, oppressed by the weight of fear; her elephants, warriors, and troops of horses all cried out.
